Fast moving waters in the Albuquerque arroyo system swept away at least two people who were rescued, while a potential third person was reported also swept away.

Several broken lines of thunderstorms in Ontario moved across and continued to develop in northern NY, some producing damaging winds or hail of one inch in diameter or greater.
episodes.202660: A cold front moved across a moderately unstable airmass across northern NY and VT during the afternoon and early evening hours on July 3rd. Several broken lines of thunderstorms moved across northern NY into VT, some producing damaging winds or hail of one inch in diameter or greater. episodes.202680: Surface cold front stationed north of the region gradually drifted southward across the northern half of Pennsylvania during the afternoon hours of July 3, 2025. A localized jet maximum stationed across the Great Lakes gradually shifted eastward in this same timeframe, allowing for portions of northeastern Pennsylvania to be stationed in the left exit region of the jet, with upward velocity in a highly unstable environment allowing for scattered convection to form. Low-level shear remained sufficient to allow for strengthening updrafts, allowing for damaging winds across portions of Tioga, Columbia, and Schuylkill counties with large hail reported in eastern Schuylkill County. Strong-to-severe thunderstorms persisted into the evening hours, knocking a tree down in Harrisburg.
episodes.202741: The combination of the subtropical high over the Four Corners/Rockies and an area of low pressure near the southern CA coastline resulted in a modest southeasterly flow that advected modest amounts of moisture across much of central and southern AZ. With the moisture advection, PWAT values increased upwards of 1.3-1.5. This moisture quantity in combination with strong daytime heating led to moderate instability as MLCAPE increased upwards of 1000 J/KG. Thunderstorm activity during the early to mid afternoon hours on the 2nd developed across the higher terrain areas of south-central and southeast AZ with outflow boundaries migrating west to northwestward into the lower deserts, where additional thunderstorm activity developed, with the heaviest activity observed across the western half of Maricopa County through the western side of the Phoenix metro area. Another isolated cluster of thunderstorms developed across central La Paz County as well. The increasing upper-level forcing from the approaching low pressure system likely enhanced the thunderstorm activity. During the afternoon hours on the 3rd, additional thunderstorm activity, although much more isolated in nature, developed across portions of south-central AZ. This activity was aided by moderate instability as MLCAPE values were around 1000-1500 J/KG and the presence of the upper-level forcing from the aforementioned low pressure system as it was traversing the region. With DCAPE values of 1000-1500 J/KG throughout the entire time period, conditions were favorable for the generation of strong downburst winds as well as dense blowing dust. With PWATs values approaching 1.5, the environment was moist enough for heavy rainfall producing thunderstorms that would result in isolated flash flooding.
episodes.202778: Strong thunderstorms developed over the area as monsoon moisture combined with an upper level low off the southern California coast.
episodes.202781: Deep tropical monsoon moisture interacted with an approaching upper level low moving towards the southern California coastline to bring strong thunderstorms and flash flooding to the region.
episodes.203163: A weak upper level ridge of high pressure was centered over Southeast Oklahoma, Southwest Arkansas, Northeast Texas, and Northwest Louisiana on July 3rd, although a weak upper level disturbance slid southeast around the ridge center across Central and Southern Arkansas  during the afternoon. Strong heating and ample low level moisture present yielded strong instability through the afternoon, with scattered showers and thunderstorms developing across portions of Southwest Arkansas, North Louisiana, and East Texas. One of these storms briefly became severe over Southwestern Natchitoches Parish, with damaging winds downing a tree just south of the Provencal community.
episodes.203244: An upper level trough brought embedded shortwaves aloft that developed thunderstorms in the region. Storms on July 1st were concentrated in Southwest MT. Coverage of thunderstorms became widespread across the region July 2nd due to better shear and moisture. The main hazards with storms were severe wind gusts.
episodes.203878: A upper level disturbance and approaching cold front interacted with a moist and unstable airmass that allowed for thunderstorm development.  Moderate shear values allowed a few of the storms to become severe, mostly across the White Mountains.
episodes.203882: A upper level disturbance and approaching cold front interacted with a moist and unstable airmass that allowed for thunderstorm development. Moderate shear values allowed a few of the storms to become severe, across West Central Maine.

episodes.204198: Deep layered troughing approached the area from the west along with a cold front at the surface. The area was able to destabilize ahead of the cold front to between 1000 and 1500 j/kg of MLCAPE. The front sparked showers and thunderstorms and with 30 to 40 kt of Effective Bulk Shear available, many of the storms became strong to severe. Single cells and multi-cell clusters were able to produce damaging wind gusts in southeast NY.

episodes.204216: Anomalously high moisture associated with the remnants of Tropical Storm Barry encouraged the development of tropical downpours across West Texas and Southeast New Mexico. These downpours resulted in Flash Flooding for portions of the area.
episodes.204391: A surface front was draped across north Florida. This feature combined with diurnal instability, weak steering flow, high moisture and warm temperatures aloft produced localized strong storms with gusty wet downbursts, heavy rainfall and frequent lightning.
episodes.204468: A passing cold front generated severe thunderstorms after the atmosphere ahead of it became unstable with high wind shear and steep temperature lapse rates. The scattered severe storms had very damaging winds, up to 100 mph as determined by a storm survey in Susquehanna County, and large hail. Numerous trees were knocked down in parts of Northeastern Pennsylvania. The survey team did note that terrain effects made the tree damage look like tornado damage in some areas but all damage was determined to be due to strong winds after accessing radar data.
episodes.204568: South to southeast flow at the surface combined with weak southerly flow aloft ahead of a west coast trough brought plenty of moisture into the Borderland with slow storm motion.  The heavy rain brought flash flooding to the recent Trout burn scar as well as along Highway 180 northwest of Deming.  An isolated severe thunderstorm brought wind damage to the Truth or Consequences area.
episodes.204622: A cold front passed through with scattered storms, some of which became severe with large hail and damaging winds. Despite earlier showers, the atmosphere still became unstable later in the morning through early afternoon. In addition, high wind shear and steep temperature lapse rates made conditions favorable for severe weather. ||Hail of 1 to 2 inches in diameter was observed from the Finger Lakes and south into New York's Southern Tier. One of the storms passed over the NWS Binghamton Forecast Office and dropped large hail on vehicles parked in the lot while also knocking down trees behind the building. A quick survey by a NWS Binghamton employee found trees stripped of their leaves and some crop damage in the Binghamton area. Due to the extensive area of hail reports and the size of the hail, the full extent of the damage to buildings, vehicles and crops is unknown and the estimated damage costs are likely underdone due to this.  In addition, the severe storms also had strong winds. There were numerous other reports for downed trees and wires. In a few cases, trees fell on cars, houses, or other buildings and often resulted in damage.
episodes.204751: Showers and thunderstorms developed ahead of a cold front during the afternoon hours on July 3, 2025 across eastern New York. Some of the storms became severe downing trees and wires, especially across areas south and east of Albany. Isolated instances of 1 inch hail was also observed.
episodes.204752: Showers and thunderstorms developed ahead of a cold front during the afternoon hours on July 3, 2025 across northwestern Connecticut. Some of the storms became severe downing trees and wires.

episodes.205304: During the late afternoon and early evening hours on July 2nd, a few pop up thunderstorms produced strong downburst winds in southeast Minnesota which resulted in localized wind damage. A few instances of downed trees along with some structural damage were reported with these storms. Additionally, small hail up to dime sized was observed as well.
episodes.205532: Morning through afternoon convection within weak to moderate deep layer west to southwest flow over the state produces a waterspout over Charlotte Harbor in Charlotte County, and a strong marine gust near the mouth of Tampa Bay.
episodes.205568: Elevated wind profiles allowed for around 30 knots of deep-layer effective shear with strong warm air advection present ahead of the upper ridge axis. Isolated storms fired along the elevated frontal zone and organized enough briefly to produce large hail.
episodes.205629: A cold front crossed Maine Thursday July 3rd, resulting in thunderstorms that developed and tracked across northern and central Maine. Storms entered north western Maine, tracking from northeastern Somerset and western Aroostook county, through the northern Aroostook and Crown of Maine region. Two specific thunderstorms produced damaging winds. One was a main cell west of the Allagash, far western northern Maine, with a small cell to the south in northern Somerset county, that tracked northeast into Aroostook, and maintained strength until getting into eastern Aroostook by Ashland and Presque Isle. This storm, alongside the damaging winds that knocked down trees, also had significant hail reports. By mid-afternoon, storm crossed into New Brunswick. The next significant thunderstorm was up in the Crown of Maine, around Fort Kent and Madawaska, which resulted in multiple downed trees and power lines. This storm also gradually moved into New Brunswick. Some dirt roads did experience some wash over in North Woods region.
episodes.205638: A weakness aloft moved across the region during early July. A couple isolated severe storms resulted.
episodes.205689: A deeply unstable air mass was in place across the area with high humidity as dewpoints rose through the upper 70s to near 80 and air temperatures warmed to near 90. This sent heat indices into the low 100s in the afternoon. While convergence was quite weak across the area, slightly backed winds across eastern Iowa provided enough focus for scattered thunderstorms development in the late afternoon and evening. With a lack of shear across the area, pulse thunderstorms were the primary mode. These storms formed and died quickly, and collapsing updrafts produced gusty winds, including a gust to 60 mph in Grundy county that resulted in tree damage.
episodes.205783: A cold front, moving through the region, was responsible for heavy rain and flash flooding.

episodes.205860: A cold front slowly sagged southward, moving into a very moist and unstable environment. This resulted in scattered showers and thunderstorms developing in portions of eastern Pennsylvania, with some severe thunderstorms producing damaging wind gusts and large hail.
episodes.205861: A cold front slowly sagged southward, moving into a very moist and unstable environment. This resulted in scattered showers and thunderstorms developing in portions of northern New Jersey, with some severe thunderstorms producing damaging wind gusts and large hail.
episodes.205883: Strong to severe thunderstorms formed along a passing cold front during the early afternoon hours on July 3. Instability and shear supported a few strong to severe thunderstorms during this time, while the cold front provided the forcing to initiate the storm development. Storms formed in the area of the central Genesee Valley and tracked southeast into the Finger Lakes. Severe thunderstorm related reports were limited to one report each of hail and damage, but as the storms continued to track southeast out of the Buffalo forecast area, the storms strengthened further.
episodes.205884: Showers and thunderstorms developed along an approaching trough early on the morning of July 3. As the thunderstorms approached the U.S. waters of Lake Ontario, they were strong enough to cause gusty winds, including a wind gust at Olcott of 38 knots. The storms then weakened as they approached and then moved onshore.
